title: Hotfix: Customer eval variance after routing-layer sampling fallthrough
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Summary: Two paying customers reported systematic evaluation drift after our runtime change that introduced a routing-layer 'sampling fallthrough' optimization. Both customers saw increased generation length and occasional spurious trailing tokens, causing automated evals to fail acceptance criteria. The behavior surfaced across Hosted and Dedicated deployments and was reproduced in a Private VPC customer environment.

What happened: In an effort to reduce cold-start latency for rare routes we added a routing-time optimization that applies a 'default sampling profile' when a model variant fallback triggers. This optimization unintentionally let the routing-layer profile override explicit per-request sampling/stop-seq semantics in a subset of traffic paths. Additionally, the fallback model variants have different stop-sequence tokenization behavior (multi-token stop sequences vs single-token), so the combination led to stop signals being ignored or applied late. The net effect: fewer stop events and longer generations vs baseline.

Customers affected:
- ACME Health (Private deployment, strict evals for clinical summarization) — observed >8% token overhead on eval suite and 12% failure rate for stop-based checks.
- RetailCo (Hosted + Dedicated hybrid) — production regressions in A/B tests, deploy paused.

Scope: Regression appears when three conditions align: (1) request hits a routing fallback (route-level model substitution), (2) routing-layer sampling fallthrough flag is enabled, and (3) target model variant has stop-sequence semantics incompatible with the profile. We estimate approx 0.6% of total traffic hit this path on average, but it concentrated on certain customers using pinned rollout policies.

Why this matters: Customer evals rely on deterministic termination behavior. These regressions break automated checks, cause support escalations, and undercut trust in patch releases. Because affected customers include Private deployments, the fix must be compatible with air‑gapped upgrade flows and not rely on control-plane changes alone.
reproduction_steps:
1) Use a client request with an explicit stop sequence (e.g., ["

## END"]). 2) Configure route to have a fallback to a lighter-weight variant (simulate routing fallback path). 3) Enable the routing-layer default sampling profile (feature-flag). 4) Send the eval prompt and compare tokenized output vs baseline where routing-layer fallthrough is disabled. Expected: stop sequence terminates output. Observed: outputs continue past stop tokens or emit partial suffixes. Reproducible locally by toggling FEATURE_ROUTING_SAMPLING_FALLTHROUGH in runtime config and running eval harness on an isolated cluster node.
mitigation:
Short-term: rolled back routing fallthrough flag for all customers on 2026-03-02 morning (hot rollback). For Hosted customers we exercised a fast rollback via control plane; for Dedicated we deployed a targeted hotfix to edge proxies; for Private customers we provided a patch bundle and assisted on-site upgrade. We also applied a parameterized guard in the routing layer that preserves explicit per-request sampling and stop-sequence fields (hotfix v1).

Customer communication: Notified ACME Health and RetailCo with incident summary, mitigation steps, and ETA for a permanent fix. Offered expanded logs and temporary conservative routing policy as workaround.

Operational: Increased noise on runtime stop-token metric dashboard and created an alert for divergence > 3% compared to baseline.
resolution_plan:
1) Root-cause patch: change the routing-layer application order so that per-request sampling/stop sequences are authoritative over any fallthrough defaults. Ensure stop-sequence normalization is applied with the target model's tokenizer before routing decisions. (Owner: Tomás)
2) Add unit + integration tests: cover multi-token stop sequences, fallback routing, and feature-flagged sampling fallthrough. Extend eval harness to include customer-specific prompt suites. (Owner: Test infra)
3) Compatibility sweep: run Private upgrade tests with the patch in an air-gapped lab and produce patch bundle + upgrade instructions. (Owner: Release Engineer)
4) Gradual rollout: canary on 5% of routing nodes, monitor stop-token termination metrics, then 25% then full.
5) Postmortem and automation: update rollout playbook to include automated rollback conditions for termination regressions.
Target release: runtime-1.21.1 patch; estimated ship 2026-03-09 if no blockers.
